newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mercedes-Benz chairman Werner steps down.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes-Benz chairman Werner steps down.

text.p: Mercedes-Benz chairman Helmut Werner, architect of the biggest strategy shift in the carmaker's history, resigned on Thursday after a prolonged struggle over reshaping parent Daimler-Benz AG.
Daimler-Benz said in a statement that Werner, who had opposed plans to legally dissolve Mercedes and make it part of Daimler, had offered his resignation to the company's four-man presidium.

The industrial group, which makes everything from cars to airplanes, said that Mercedes was to become part of the Daimler group, represented by three executives on the board - one for cars, one for trucks and one for marketing.
Werner approved of the plans, but quit because he felt there was no room in the reorganised group for a man with his experience, Daimler said.

The German press had been rife with talk about Werner's resignation for months with much of the speculation centring around reports of a power struggle between Werner and Daimler group chairman Juergen Schrempp.

Daimler officials have maintained they wanted Werner to remain after the restructuring, but said it was not logical for Mercedes, which is responsible for about 70 percent of the group's revenues, to remain an independent company.
